_comment: Shared visual vocabulary for the field_3d lorentz_force_uniform_field scenario. Grounded in THE EYE's baseline frames (viewed 2026-08-18), not guessed. The AI tutor has no vision — this text is the only thing it knows about the picture. A concept's own `stage` block extends this and wins on any conflicting `looks_like`.
viewpoint: The view is a 3D space seen from a camera the student can orbit — dragging rotates the view and scrolling zooms. The space is filled with a grid of blue arrows that all point the same way; that grid IS the uniform magnetic field. It is NOT a circuit: there is no battery, no wire, no resistor, no meter with a needle anywhere. Nothing here is the inside of a wire — one single charged particle (a proton) moves through empty space.

elements.looks_like: a grid of many blue arrows filling the whole space, all pointing the same way (upward)
elements.means: the uniform magnetic field B. Every arrow shows the field's direction at that point. The arrows never move — the field is constant everywhere.

elements.looks_like: one glowing orange-yellow ball with a plus sign on it
elements.means: the proton — the moving charged particle. The badge on it shows the sign of its charge; it changes to a minus sign if the charge is flipped to negative.

elements.looks_like: an orange arrow attached to the ball, labelled v
elements.means: the proton's velocity — the direction it is moving right now.

elements.looks_like: a green arrow attached to the ball, labelled F
elements.means: the magnetic force on the proton. It only appears when the force is not zero, and it always points at a right angle to both v and the blue field arrows.

elements.looks_like: a pale line trailing behind the ball
elements.means: the path the proton has traced. Its shape is the whole lesson: a straight line when v is along the field, a circle when v is across the field, and a spiral (helix) in between.

elements.looks_like: small pale spheres spaced along the circular path (in the circle state)
elements.means: markers dropped at equal time intervals. Their equal spacing is the proof that the speed never changes — the magnetic force turns the proton but never speeds it up or slows it down.

elements.looks_like: a 3D human right hand floating near the particle (in the right-hand-rule state only)
elements.means: the right-hand rule model: fingers point along v, curl toward B, and the thumb gives the direction of the force F.

elements.looks_like: grey and peach arrows labelled v cos θ and v sin θ (in the helix state only)
elements.means: the two parts of the velocity: v cos θ runs along the field and drifts freely, v sin θ runs across the field and gets turned in a circle. Together they make the helix.

elements.looks_like: a panel in the top right corner with sliders and a small +e badge
elements.means: the controls: charge sign (+e or −e, click to flip), speed |v| in units of 10^5 m/s, field strength B in millitesla, and the angle θ between v and B in degrees. Different states show different sliders.

elements.looks_like: a green line of text in the top-right panel reading F = some number fN
elements.means: the live force readout, in femtonewtons. It updates as the sliders move; it reads exactly zero when v is along the field.

elements.looks_like: a short label in the bottom left corner, with 'Drag to rotate, Scroll to zoom' under it
elements.means: the name of what this state is showing, and a reminder that the 3D view itself can be turned with the mouse.
